profile-list.title: Saved profile
profile-list.text: Select a profile to edit its current revision, or choose New profile. Saved optimizer runs retain their own frozen revision even after you edit or remove this profile.

profile-name.title: Profile name
profile-name.text: A descriptive name for this plant's settings, such as a site and planning season. You can keep multiple named profiles for the same plant.

profile-plant.title: Plant
profile-plant.text: Use the exact plant identifier from your published dataset. The workspace offers datasets containing this plant and checks the demand horizon before creating a run.

horizon_days.title: Horizon (demand days)
horizon_days.text: Number of demand days represented by the uploaded forecast. Daily demand equals forecast litres divided by this number. Match the source workbook: the Q4 source uses 80 demand days, while the original annual source uses 250. Changing this field does not convert or rescale a forecast. A mismatch blocks the run.

demand_days_per_week.title: Demand days per week
demand_days_per_week.text: Converts the demand horizon into productive weeks for the within-group changeover proxy: weeks = horizon / days per week. At 5 days per week, an 80-day forecast covers 16 weeks. This is not a line-capacity or shift schedule.

high_runner_threshold_days.title: High-runner threshold
high_runner_threshold_days.text: Exactly two classes: high when individual reference coverage is less than or equal to this cutoff, low when greater. The default is 15 days, including exactly 15. There is no medium class. Rules using strict less-than require clarification if they disagree with this inclusive setting.

runner_basis.title: Runner basis
runner_basis.text: Fixed source reference uses the source lot size considered divided by the product's daily demand, without applying another 0.90 factor. Candidate PV uses the candidate production version's effective batch divided by that individual product's daily demand, as if produced alone. Candidate PV is a sensitivity setting and may change a product's class between production versions; it does not classify using the combined group's demand.

matrix_mode.title: Compatibility mode
matrix_mode.text: Y pairs are compatible. N pairs are forbidden in every mode. HARD also rejects AVOID pairs. FLEXIBLE permits AVOID pairs and reports them. DIAGNOSTIC prioritizes fewer AVOID pairs before its other objectives. OFF does not add an AVOID preference, but still respects explicit N prohibitions. Volume compatibility does not override filling-line eligibility.

maximum_group_size.title: Maximum group size
maximum_group_size.text: Maximum number of products in a subgroup for this plant profile. A specific rule can impose a tighter cap, such as two products for groups eligible for line 6. This field is a hard limit, not a target number of products.

rules-text.title: Fixed plant rules
rules-text.text: Only enter rules that every run using this profile must follow. Test alternative grouping strategies in separate workspace runs. Describe volume compatibility here as an alternative to Excel: list compatible volume families and explicitly state whether other pairs are forbidden or discouraged. Preview the interpretation, resolve every clarification and Accept any proposed matrix before saving. Undefined similarity, alternative strategies and soft preferences must not silently become hard rules. A line-eligibility cap does not itself prefer assigning that line; an explicit workspace objective is needed. The changeover proxy omits initial and between-group setups, so zero proxy does not mean zero real plant changeovers.
